public_rationale: Public text-to-video counterparts emerged after the post. Open-Sora recorded a March 2024 release, and its December paper documented public code and weights. Wan released inference code and weights on February 25, 2025, with runnable text-to-video models and an Apache 2.0 license. These releases settle the existence forecast under the ordinary functional reading of 'counterparts.' They do not establish the surrounding predictions about scammers, advertising, or educational harm.
limitations: The conclusion depends on interpreting counterparts functionally, without an unstated requirement for Sora-level performance.
Open-source here means accessible code and weights under an open-source license, not a fully disclosed training dataset.
No precise deadline can fairly be assigned to 'In short order.'

our_interpretation: Assess only the supplied proposition that open-source counterparts to Sora will emerge, not the surrounding predictions about scammers or advertising.
The plain reading of counterparts is publicly usable models with the same core text-to-video function. It does not require identical video quality, duration, or benchmark performance.
Read open-source as public model weights and runnable source code under an open-source license. Complete disclosure of the training dataset is not an added requirement.
The surrounding phrase 'In short order' expresses urgency but supplies no calendar deadline for this proposition.
criteria.support_condition: Dated primary records establish public releases after February 18, 2024 of text-to-video models with downloadable weights and runnable source code under open-source licenses.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A decisive barrier establishes that such counterparts cannot emerge. Failure to find a release by an evaluator-selected date cannot contradict this forecast without a stated deadline.
